bibliographic.title: The HoPE Model Architecture: a Novel Approach to Pregnancy Information Retrieval Based on Conversational Agents
bibliographic.authors: João Luis Zeni Montenegro; Cristiano André da Costa
bibliographic.citation_apa: Montenegro, J. L. Z., & da Costa, C. A. (2022). The HoPE Model Architecture: a Novel Approach to Pregnancy Information Retrieval Based on Conversational Agents. Journal of Healthcare Informatics Research, 6, 253–294. https://doi.org/10.1007/s41666-022-00115-0

methodology.study_design: technical architecture study with dataset construction and benchmark comparison
methodology.sample_description: Collections of health documents related to breastfeeding, childcare, pregnant care, nutrition, risks, vaccines, exams, and physical exercises; fine-tuning with 1,500 pairs
methodology.sample_size: 1,500 pairs for fine-tuning; full corpus size unclear
methodology.technology_context: Conversational agent using BERTimbau/Sentence-BERT, rule-based dialogue, NLP machine learning engines, ontology-oriented dialogs, knowledge base, and information retrieval for pregnancy questions in Portuguese

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study proposes and evaluates a pregnancy-focused conversational agent architecture using BERTimbau and information retrieval; it does not address conversational governance, accountability, oversight, audit, compliance, guardrails, or LLM-based systems.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the article is clearly about conversational agents in a regulated healthcare domain, the provided text shows a pre-LLM technical architecture and performance evaluation paper (F1-Score, Spearman correlation) rather than governance of conversational AI. GPT-3 appears only as background literature, not as the implemented system. No governance, human oversight, monitoring, audit, compliance, or accountability mechanisms are described as study objectives or contributions.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage marked borderline_manual (84.67, grade B) because conversational and regulated-domain signals are strong, but governance signals are weak; full-text review confirms technical CA focus without governance or LLM specificity.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on provided excerpts. The objective and evaluation metrics are clear, but ethics, limitations, and full sampling details are only partially visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: For the review question on conversational governance in LLM-based regulated systems, relevance is low because the article centers on a BERT-based retrieval architecture and performance benchmarking, not governance mechanisms or LLM deployment controls.

coding.theme: Conversational agent architecture for pregnancy information retrieval
coding.subtheme: Hybrid dialogue design with rules, NLP engines, ontology, and knowledge base

synthesis.main_claim: The authors propose the HoPE architecture, a pregnancy-focused conversational agent information retrieval system using BERTimbau with data augmentation, reporting strong retrieval performance (F1-Score 0.89).
synthesis.contribution: Provides a domain-tailored conversational agent architecture and comparative evaluation for Portuguese pregnancy health information retrieval using transformer-based embeddings rather than governance frameworks.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text indicates future clinical evaluation is still needed; broader limitations, ethics, and operational governance are not described in the excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance in LLM-regulated settings; at most foundational contextual background on healthcare conversational agents and knowledge-base-driven dialogue design.

evidence.claim: Study objective is to evaluate and propose a pregnancy-tailored conversational agent model
evidence.excerpt: The main goal of this study is to evaluate and propose a HoPE (Healthcare Obstetric in PrEgnancy) model that is tailored to pregnancy data.
The HoPE model architecture achieved an F1-Score of 0.89, outperforming other combinations tested in this study.

evidence.claim: Implemented technology is BERTimbau-based, not an LLM governance system
evidence.excerpt: We evaluated two pre-trained models in the Portuguese language for the conversational agent architecture proposal and chose the one with the best performance to compose the HoPE architecture.
dataset extraction and construction process based on collections of health documents related to breastfeeding, childcare, pregnant care, nutrition, risks, vaccines, exams, and physical exercises

evidence.claim: Dialog architecture combines rules, NLP ML, and ontology with knowledge base
evidence.excerpt: The dialog structure proposed by HoPE uses a composite of pre-defined rules, NLP machine learning engines, and ontology-oriented dialogs.

evidence.claim: Knowledge base is part of the conversational support stack
evidence.excerpt: Prenatal Labor Postpartum NLP Interface NLU Ontology Information Retrieval Dictionary of Synonyms Knowledge Base

evidence.claim: GPT-3 is cited only in background literature, not as the studied system
evidence.excerpt: Many architectures such as GPT-3 [32], BERT [27], and ELMO [75] have already been used frequently in recent studies.

evidence.claim: No governance, oversight, audit, or compliance focus is stated in provided text
evidence.excerpt: We will evaluate this approach for clinical studies in future studies.
